title: Paloma and the Safehouse
premise: Lior Thornbury guards a safe house for a witness protection client who never speaks, haunted by the night his last detail ended in fire. When the property appears on a real estate site with interior photos — including the hidden room and the client's face half-turned to the window — Lior realizes someone inside the program is selling them out. As he traces the leak through a broker, a burned-out handler, and his own fractured memory of 'the incident,' he discovers the scheduled attack will be staged as a gas explosion during an inspection visit. In the end Lior chooses exposure over invisibility: he burns his own cover identity to move the client out ahead of the strike, confronts the handler who orchestrated it all, and finds that the found family he built in hiding — the client, a teenage neighbor, and a disgraced analyst — is the only identity worth keeping.
about_author: Jonah Villalobos is a former logistics coordinator for private security firms who writes thrillers about the people paid to stay unseen. He lives near the coast with his partner and a dog named after a safe house.

chapters.title: The House That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A routine night shift at the safe house establishes his insomnia, his silent client 'Mara,' and the rules of invisibility. The emotional beat is brittle vigilance — Lior checks locks three times because sleep means remembering the fire.

chapters.title: Listed
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A neighbor's teenage son, Dev, shows him a real estate listing with photos of the interior — Mara's silhouette in a window, the reinforced door. Lior's panic collides with the realization that the breach came from inside the program. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Mara Speaks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins with Mara. She breaks her silence just enough to say she recognizes the photographer's angle — it was taken from her old family home. Emotional beat: two guarded people negotiating trust over instant coffee at 3 a.m.

chapters.title: The Handler
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He contacts Wren Okafor, the program handler who went dark after the incident, and gets stonewalled — but notices Wren's name on the listing's brokerage paperwork. Beat: betrayal as vertigo; the man who taught Lior tradecraft may be selling it.

chapters.title: Inspection Day
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A gas company inspection arrives weeks early, friendly and wrong. Lior stalls them while Mara copies the inspector's work order — dated for a return visit, signed by someone using Lior's own old credentials. Beat: the trap has his fingerprints on it.

chapters.title: What Lior Remembers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, fragmented flashbacks. Reconstructing the incident, he realizes the fire that killed his last principal was also staged as an accident — same signature, same handler. Beat: grief reframed as evidence; his guilt was manufactured.

chapters.title: Dev's Garage
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV shifts. The team coalesces in the neighbor's garage: Dev runs the digital trace, disgraced analyst Priya decodes the listing metadata, Mara maps escape routes from memory. Beat: warmth under pressure — found family forming in a place built for no one.

chapters.title: The Broker's Price
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He meets the listing broker posing as a buyer and learns the sale closes the morning of the second inspection — the attack date. Wren surfaces, warning Lior off, half apology, half threat. Beat: the clock becomes audible.

chapters.title: Gas
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax. Inspection day: Lior moves Mara out through the storm drain while Priya triggers a false alarm that empties the block. Wren's crew detonates the empty house; Lior stays behind to record Wren confessing the whole operation. Beat: sacrifice of safety for truth.

chapters.title: Paloma
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, then Lior's. The recording lands; Wren is taken, and Mara reveals her real name — Paloma — choosing identity over erasure. Lior sleeps through the night for the first time in years, in a borrowed room full of people who stayed. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
